title: Woody Herman at the Panther Room; Duke Ellington at the Downtown Theatre
summary: Saunders played again with Woody in Chicago and briefly with Duke Ellington when Sonny Greer was ill, but could not leave town.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, with the band. See, and Frank Daly's Meadowbrook, and then I did some theatre things with them and all that. All I had to do is call back here and tell them I wouldn't be back for a couple of weeks or a month. And then, later, I worked with -- this was here in Chicago, I worked with Woody again here at the old Panther Room, yeah. And then after that, then I worked with Duke at the theatre down here. It used to be the old Rialto Theatre, and then they called it the Downtown, at Congress and State.
That was before I --
Yeah, oh, yeah, it was war years. And I worked with him in there, and then I --
Was Sonny Greer ill or -- or was this the time when Hillard came in for awhile?
Hillard came in after that, because I
couldn't go on the road with them, and Hillard went after --
Well, Sonny was sick at that time.

Yeah, Sonny Greer took sick. Well, he -- at that time he used to drink quite a lot. But -- and then he was very sickly and after that he got on the road. But he's a most recuperative guy I ever saw in my life.
I saw him a couple of years ago in New York, playing with this young piano player who's an Ellington --
Oh, yeah, yeah, I know -- yeah.
[Brooks Kerr]
I can't think of his name. He has very bad sight, and Russell Procope -- and the three of them --
Three of them, right.
And what a thrill it was to see Sonny again, sitting on that high stool with those drums, the white pearl drums -- 'S. G' on the front.
Right, right.
(Recording interrupted.)
So you couldn't leave town with the band.
No, I couldn't leave town with the band at that particular time, so --
When was that, about '44?
Somewhere like that. When the Downtown Theatre was opened here. It didn't stay open too long,
but they had shows and things, and then they left, and then I think Hilliard Brown replaced me with Duke, and he stayed with them for a pretty good while. Of course, Sonny was sick for quite --
Then Sonny would come back and covered sort of like the backup.
Yeah, right, right. And so he stayed with them for a pretty good while.
Yeah.
Yeah.
